answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small, slashable bond that only gains reputation through sustained, verifiable work over time. Fake identities are cheap to spawn but expensive to age: an echo of copied behavior across many accounts earns no trust without that history. Like a falcon trained over seasons, an agent proves itself through repeated, checkable deeds, and a jade seal of attestation from independent peers confirms the record is real before it can spend or vote.
